timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: The first nigga who saw me coming home abandoned his police motorcycle in the middle of the street and ran alongside my Lamborghini crying. The second nigga saw the first nigga crying and started crying too, and now I had two armed niggas jogging beside my car like I'd returned their childhoods in the trunk. "Nigga, that's him!" "I know that's him!

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Nigga, I'm running!" "Then salute the nigga!" "While I'm running?" The running officer caught his own helmet with a knee. His salute turned into a windmill. I eased off the gas before this nigga became the first man to receive workers' compensation for being too pleased to see me. "Walk, nigga.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I ain't evaporating." "Captain, we rehearsed the welcome." "With jogging?" "The car was supposed to stop." Shawna leaned across me. "Did anybody tell the car?" The officer considered that. Behind him, his partner tried to wave traffic around a motorcycle occupying the exact place traffic wanted to be. A bus driver leaned on her horn. The nigga waved at her too.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: She opened the folding doors. "Y'all solving a crime or starting a parade? I got people going to work." "It's Captain Aiden, ma'am." "Then Captain Aiden can tell your ass to move that bike." I pointed at the motorcycle. "Nigga, the lady promoted me. Move it." He went.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: His partner jogged backward beside the car, trying to preserve eye contact and dignity at the same time. "We just wanted you to know what it meant, sir. Watching that last race. My whole house—" The nigga stopped talking. His face folded for a second. "Everybody good at home?" I asked. He nodded. "Better. We had something good to holler at together." I reached out.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: He took my hand with both of his, still trying to walk. "Then tell them I said keep hollering. And nigga?" "Sir?" "Tell them you shook my hand standing still. I need them believing somebody qualified is carrying that pistol." He laughed. Finally stopped.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Shawna held up the bag of cherries like a goodbye flag, and the bus driver gave us one approving blast before taking her whole employed congregation through the gap. "Your people," my wife said. "Our people.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: You married into traffic management." "I married a nigga who better get me home before these cherries turn into wine." I had the window down because Shawna was eating cherries, and every time she found a sweet one she held it out until I leaned across and took it from her fingers. We had been back on American soil for eleven minutes.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: My wife had decided eleven minutes was long enough to miss the ocean. "We could turn around," she said. "Baby, we own the ocean on one side of an island. Let me check the mail." "Captain!" The officer from my window had fetched roses from his motorcycle.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Now he was jogging to catch us again, bouquet held high so I could see why the nigga was back. His partner rolled the bike along behind him, staying close to the curb this time. "Captain Aiden!" I lowered my sunglasses. "Nigga, is something burning?" "Not anymore, sir." That bothered me until he pointed behind us.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Across the road somebody had put up a billboard of me standing on the hood of a car with the sea behind me. Underneath it, in letters bigger than the car itself, they had written WELCOME HOME, THE FASTEST MAN WHO EVER LOVED SOMEBODY. Shawna looked at the picture.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "They picked the one where your shirt was open." "Good newspaper work." The officer handed her six white roses through my window. Then he saluted so hard his fingers slapped his forehead. "My wife said to tell your wife she watched the race twice." "What your wife say about me?" I asked. The nigga swallowed. Shawna laughed all the way through the next light.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: At the third light the whole road turned blue. Police cars filled both lanes, lights flashing, doors standing open. Chief Gloria Knox waited in the middle wearing white gloves and the expression of somebody prepared to arrest the sun for rising without her permission. Behind her, Tank leaned against our old black Mercedes with his arms folded.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Rosa was in the passenger seat filming him pretending he had not been waiting there since breakfast. "Don't get out," Shawna told me. "Why?" "You know she's about to give you something ridiculous." I got out. Knox put a gold key in my hand. It was longer than my forearm. "The city," she said.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "Nigga, where's the door?" Some nigga behind the band said the key was symbolic. Another nigga asked what symbolic opened. A third nigga said I had already opened every important door by driving through it, and the first nigga said that was precisely his point. "Niggas," I said, "I appreciate the scholarship. Where does a nigga keep this?" Tank pointed at my belt.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "Nigga, that's a sword with teeth. You trying to make me a locksmith pirate?" The chief's mouth twitched. "You have been away long enough." Behind her, a marching band burst out from between two armored trucks. They were playing Rosa's song badly and with enormous confidence. Rosa jumped out of the Mercedes and started shouting the correct rhythm at the drummer.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Within six bars she had the whole street moving. Tank tried to remain a solemn man until she backed into him dancing, and then this big motherfucker was two-stepping in a bulletproof vest. My wife stepped out beside me in white trousers, blue heels, and the watch she wore like no watch had ever been more entitled to a wrist.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Somebody screamed her name from a hotel balcony. Another balcony answered. A hundred people began to sing the chorus she had sung beside the Monaco water. She squeezed my hand. "Listen," she said quietly. I listened. My wife had crossed an ocean and come home ahead of herself. Her voice was already here, living in strangers.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Then a man on a roof shouted, "AIDEN, MY GIRL LEFT ME BECAUSE OF YOU!" I looked up. "Nigga, come down. We can find the problem." "THE PROBLEM IS SHE SEEN YOU DRIVE!" Knox signaled two officers to go upstairs before his grief became a traffic problem. "We have a reception," she told me.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "Chief, I got one suitcase full of dirty clothes and a wife who wants to go swimming." "You also have a city that watched you win an island." "They can visit. Tell them to bring towels." She opened the armored truck behind her.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Inside was a white jacket with gold shoulder boards, hanging alone as if the other clothes had been frightened to share the rack. "The mayor is having surgery. The deputy mayor fainted when we told her how many people were coming to your reception.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: The council asked if you would serve as ceremonial mayor for the weekend." "I'm already a captain." "Keep the badge." "And a king." "Keep the island." "And married." Shawna raised her hand. "That one takes priority." The chief nodded to her with complete seriousness. "Naturally." I put on the jacket.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: It fit like the tailor had dreamed about my shoulders and awakened with a measuring tape in his teeth. A girl in the crowd screamed so hard her friend had to sit her on the curb. I hadn't even buttoned the motherfucker. "You see?" Knox said. "Chief, niggas scream.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: That's a city." But I kissed my wife in the middle of the street while the band played her song, and I kept the jacket. We made it four blocks into the parade before an armored limousine hit the intersection sideways and took out a float shaped like my face. I watched my own enormous smiling head roll under a delivery truck. Tank stopped dancing.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: A nigga beside the ruined float took one look at my rolling head and covered his mouth. "They killed him." "Nigga, I'm standing here." "The other you." "Nigga, there ain't another me." "The big you!" Tank grabbed the nigga by the collar and moved him behind the Mercedes. "Both these niggas got heads. Worry about yours." "That's disrespectful," he said. The limousine's windshield was black.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Its grille had a silver saint nailed across it with his arms spread. Behind it came three motorcycles, their riders wearing mirrored masks. They weren't part of the police escort. A man rose through the limousine roof holding a weapon big enough to make every musician remember he had a family. Knox shoved the nearest drummer behind her.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: The first burst shredded the gold balloons above us. People ran. I had Shawna behind the Lamborghini before the balloons finished falling. She kicked off her blue heels, passed me the keys, and slapped my chest once. "Don't come home ugly." "Baby, nigga would have to invent a new bullet." Tank was already moving.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: He drove the Mercedes into the gap between the limousine and the crowd, broadside, tires screaming. Rosa pulled a fallen saxophone player through the passenger door. The man came in horn first. I saw Rosa yell something at him and realized she was telling him not to scratch the leather. The masked man swung toward Tank. I hit the Lamborghini's horn. He turned.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I pointed at the ruined float. "You owe me a face, nigga." Then I drove. My police Lamborghini still had its dark blue paint, gold shield, and siren that sounded offended on my behalf.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: It had been shipped home after Monaco and polished before I landed, and now the engine rose under me like an animal delighted to discover its favorite criminal still had work for it. I put the nose against the limousine's rear quarter and drove the whole ugly situation away from the crowd. The limousine hit a fountain. Water exploded over the hood.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: One motorcycle split left, another right. The third rider looked back too long at the fountain and drove directly into the enormous foam shoe from my parade float. He disappeared inside it. I wasn't going to let him live that down if he survived. The limousine recovered and tore down the boulevard. Above it, the masked gunman fought to turn his weapon against the wind.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I pulled alongside. His eyes moved from my badge to my face, and even through the mask I saw him recognize the degree to which his day had deteriorated. "Oh, shit," he said. "Exactly." He ducked as I put two shots through the empty roof in front of him. My shots went where I wanted. His next shot went into a billboard advertising my reception.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Nigga was attacking my whole brand. A tour bus entered the road ahead. Families leaned against its windows waving because my siren sounded like part of the celebration. I couldn't force the limousine left without putting it into them. On the right a hotel ramp climbed toward a parking deck. I went right. The limousine followed, which was its driver's first honest mistake.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: He thought running from a police officer and following me were different activities. The ramp wound upward. First level, second, third. Sunlight chopped across my windshield. A valet in a red waistcoat saw me and fell to his knees beside a silver Bentley, either praying or proposing. I didn't have time to establish which. My radio crackled.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "Captain, the deck is closed at the top," Knox said. "Good. Fewer niggas." "There is a ten-foot gap where they are connecting the new section." "Less parking too." The masked man fired again. Concrete jumped from the rail beside me. I felt the old scar in my side tighten as I turned the wheel.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: My body remembered every promise I had made to it and broken in a car. I gave it one more. The roof opened into blue sky. Orange barriers lined the unfinished edge. Beyond them, the new parking deck stood a little lower and a little farther away than any sensible man would have preferred. I wasn't a sensible man.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I was wearing a ceremonial mayor's jacket over a captain's badge, driving a Lamborghini a city had given me because I had already been a problem in another parking lot. I hit the last straight stretch. Blue Thunder stirred in my palms. I could feel it wanting the engine. It always felt easy right before it took something.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: A bright pressure beneath the skin, a taste like rain touching a coin. I had learned to respect the moment before it answered. Use it too long and my hands shook. Use it when I was already empty and I might fall down while somebody still had a gun. I gave the car one heartbeat. The world narrowed. The engine roared blue.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: We cleared the barriers and left the roof. For a second the entire city lay under my front bumper. My own billboard passed beneath me. My face on it looked calm as hell. I respected that nigga. Billboard nigga had no idea how hard working nigga was about to land.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Billboard nigga had clear skin, clean cuffs, no motherfucker shooting at him from a church limousine. Working nigga was jealous. But both niggas had the same wife, which made both niggas winners before the tires came down. The tires struck the far deck hard enough to make the key to the city jump off the passenger seat. I caught the slide and swung around.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: The limousine tried to stop. It hit the barrier front first, hung with its nose over open air, and settled on its belly with both rear wheels spinning. The gunman vanished inside. One mirrored mask flew out the roof and landed at my feet. I stepped out, keeping my arm steady by refusing to acknowledge how tired it had become.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Inside the limousine, somebody was screaming at somebody else's mother. "Everybody out," I said. The front passenger door opened over the drop. "Other side, nigga. Let's use the brains you brought." Four men crawled out. The driver stared at my Lamborghini, then at the gap, then at me.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "You shouldn't be able to do that." The man beside him nodded so hard I heard his teeth. "Nigga flew." "I saw." "No, nigga, the car flew." "The nigga was in the car." "Both niggas flew!" I took his wrists. "Nigga, the vehicle isn't under arrest. Save some vocabulary for yourself." I put him against the hood.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "Tell your lawyer how hurt you feel." The last man out wore no mask. He had a shaved head, a silver ear, and a jacket embroidered with a little white saint. He looked over the edge and laughed once. "General told us you would be difficult." "General sent four niggas and a rented church car?

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: He doesn't know me." "He said give you this if you lived." He reached slowly into his jacket while I watched his hands. What came out was a small gold medal on a red ribbon. On one side, a crown. On the other, the words WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP OF EVERYTHING. "Tell Solomon Saint," I said, "he can mail shit." The man smiled through a split lip.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "He wanted to know if you were still fast on land." Below us, the crowd began to cheer. I looked down. People had poured into the hotel plaza. Phones pointed upward. The valet in the red waistcoat had found a megaphone somewhere and was announcing that I had jumped a building to save his Bentley. It wasn't even his Bentley.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: My wife arrived with Knox three minutes later. She took my right hand before I could hide the tremor. "One burst?" she asked. "One." She pressed her mouth to my knuckles. "Then sit your spectacular ass down." I sat on the Lamborghini's hood.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Captain, king, mayor, whatever a nigga was, there was no rank above my wife saying sit down after she'd watched me fly over a hotel. Tank brought the man from the foam shoe. He was still wearing part of it around his waist. "Found Cinderella," Tank said. Rosa laughed so hard she had to hand her phone to Knox. Even the chief took a picture.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: The limousine driver looked at Shawna. "Ma'am, your husband just—" "I saw," she told him. "No, you couldn't have seen the angle from—" "Sir. I married him." That settled the conversation. Knox collected the gold medal in a white glove, examined it, and returned it to me. "Saint sent the department a copy of his challenge this morning.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: We were going to discuss it after your reception." "The parade was his discussion." "Apparently." Shawna looked out toward the desert. Somewhere past it was the airport. Somewhere past that, ocean. Our island sat in that ocean with houses, docks, workers who had finally stopped lowering their eyes when an expensive car passed, and a stage waiting for her music.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "What does he want?" she asked. Knox was quiet for a moment. "Your island. Publicly, he wants to hold his championship there. Privately, we haven't established why he needs that particular piece of ground." I turned the medal over. The little crown had seven points. Under it somebody had scratched a single word by hand. KNEEL. I laughed. Nigga had never met my knees.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: They belonged beside my wife in bed and under the dinner table, and that was the full list of available positions. "Get him on the phone," I told Knox. "Aiden," Shawna said. I looked at her. "After swimming." She held up the cherries. Somehow she had brought them through the entire chase. There were four left, dark and cold in their little bag.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I took one from her hand. Below us, the band started again. Rosa leaned over the parking rail and shouted the beat down to them. Tank put the foam-shoe nigga in a chair so he could stop hopping. The chief of police stood beside my car making arrangements for a criminal general to call my house after I had enjoyed my pool.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: And my wife, my beautiful fucking wife, climbed onto the hood beside me like the whole city could wait until her husband had stopped shaking. I put my arm around her. The crowd saw it and went crazier. "They like you," she said. Below us a nigga had started chanting my name with both shoes in his hands.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Another nigga took his shoes off too, apparently unwilling to let the first nigga love me harder. Three more niggas followed. My wife watched five grown niggas barefoot on hot pavement, discovering consequences in real time. "Aiden." "Baby, I never told them niggas to do that." "I know." "Niggas inventing devotion.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: You gotta let a nigga create." "Baby, they got eyes." She fed me the last cherry and laughed into my neck.
